headline_marked: UK military [[jamming foreign satellites]] to defend against threats
headline: UK military jamming foreign satellites to defend against threats
summary: The Royal Air Force has deployed a ground-based system to block adversary satellites, a move confirmed by defense sources over the past year.
details: The British military has been actively jamming or blocking satellites belonging to other nations as a defensive measure against potential threats. This capability, utilized by the RAF over the past year, is understood to prevent hostile satellites from tracking sensitive UK military operations, including nuclear submarine movements and special forces activities.

This action coincides with the creation of a new RAF unit, the Space Effects Squadron, tasked with "disrupting, degrading and denying hostile threats in space." The head of the RAF highlighted the unprecedented threats faced in space, emphasizing the growing scale, speed, and sophistication of these challenges.

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting underscored the critical reliance of daily life and the economy on satellites, noting that a loss of GPS alone would cost the UK economy £1.4 billion per day. He stated that this dependency makes space a prime target for adversaries.

The UK's terrestrial electronic warfare capability is described as "world leading." This development follows a confirmation from the US that it has also deployed a defensive "weapon" in space. Both China and Russia have condemned such actions, warning of a potential space arms race.

Nations are believed to possess similar ground-based satellite jamming systems. Last year, Russia was reported to be attempting to jam UK satellites weekly with such systems. The RAF has also tracked dangerous maneuvers by Russian satellites and noted disruptions to GPS signals across Europe and Canada.

headline: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT Voice with three new capabilities
summary: ChatGPT's voice interaction is getting a significant boost with new features rolling out today, enhancing user experience and functionality.
details: OpenAI has announced a series of three key improvements to ChatGPT's voice capabilities, making interactions more natural and efficient.
These updates aim to enhance the conversational experience, allowing users to interact with ChatGPT more seamlessly through voice commands.
While specific details on each of the three new capabilities are still emerging, the focus is on improving the overall utility and responsiveness of the voice feature.
This move signifies OpenAI's continued commitment to advancing AI accessibility and user-friendly interfaces across its platforms, including the popular ChatGPT mobile app.
